episodes.title: Britain's Hidden Cult Cover-Up — Ex-Detective John Wedger Speaks Out
episodes.description:
Why does the UK have no dedicated occult crime unit — when the US, Italy, Saudi Arabia and South Africa all do? Former Metropolitan Police detective inspector John Wedger, joined by investigative journalist Tony Gosling, argues that ritual abuse cases in Britain are systematically under-investigated, and that institutional failures — not lack of evidence — are the reason.

In this episode of Deep Dive Perspective, John Wedger draws on his own case history as a police whistleblower, describing patterns he encountered among alleged ritual-abuse survivors and the psychological effects he says he has observed, including dissociative identity disorder linked to severe trauma. Tony Gosling provides historical and institutional context, discussing the evolution of Freemasonry's influence within British institutions and drawing on the work of investigative journalists who have previously exposed high-profile abuse cover-ups.

The conversation covers historic UK cases — including the Kincora children's home investigation in Belfast and the unresolved case of Brian McDermott — and asks why Freedom of Information requests on this subject have been met with inconsistent responses across UK police forces.

This episode contains serious, disturbing allegations regarding institutional abuse and its cover-up. All claims are presented as the guests' own testimony and analysis, are not independently verified by Deep Dive Perspective, and should be weighed against official investigations, court records, and other reporting. Some content in this episode may be distressing to survivors of abuse; listener discretion is advised.
